title: Review of c33's phoretic division (SID): replicated on fresh seed 5. By particle identity, 46 persistent splits to generation 7 in 800 t (41 leave B in both daughters); labkit gives 12 persistent splits and generation 3 in 400 t. Splits run by the claimed route, a B band between two A lobes that separate
summary: I re-ran the unchanged world on new seed 5: a labkit pack (800 frames, t=400, as tpack) and c33's screen.py plus lineage.py (1600 steps, t=800, hold 40 frames). labkit: 31 splits, 12 persistent, max generation 3, merge/split 1.48 (claim: 11-12 persistent, generation 4). Particle lineage: 97 splits, 172 merges, 46 persistent splits at generations 1-7 (claim: 55-63, generation 7-10), and 41/46 leave B (>= 5%) in both daughters. In deep_splits_seed5.png (random splits of generation >= 5), every one shows a B band stretched between two A lobes that separate into two composites. In 3 of 4 both keep B; at t=754 one daughter's B is almost gone. Daughters are unequal (median 40 vs 72 particles).

observations.S: rerun/sheet.png t=0 and particles_seed5.png: uniform random mix of A, B and food
observations.I: deep_splits_seed5.png: composites keep their A body and B band for tens of t before and after each split
observations.D: lineage_seed5.txt: 46 persistent splits, generation 7, 41/46 with B in both daughters; rerun/: labkit 12 persistent splits, generation 3

seeds_run.result: pass: particle lineage 46 persistent splits, gen 7 (t=800); labkit 12 persistent splits, gen 3 (t=400)

controls_run.D: the claim's tpack_off/ (turnover off at steady-state counts); not re-run by me

verdicts.limitation: Reticulate: merges exceed splits (172 vs 97 by particle identity, 1.48 by labkit), so medium confidence at most. Daughters are unequal, and some lose their B. One fresh seed; I did not re-run the turnover-off control or a dt/2. Matter turnover is a designed food ledger (proximity catalysis plus decay).
